implementation_refinements: Four transition rules also cover INSERT: schema_definitions, ocr_runs, review_runs, review_attempts; names and rule count retained.
Project lock/requery paths explicitly support READ COMMITTED and reject other isolation modes; FOR NO KEY UPDATE remains compatible with FK key-share locks.
Attempt UPDATE already locks its target before its BEFORE trigger. Future entry points must prelock run then attempt; triggers alone do not establish caller lock order.
Historical tests compare copied metadata stripped only of later indexes; frozen old migration sources remain unchanged.
limitations: M007 is complete for C07b but M008 column/table/function privileges and final readiness are pending C07c. App writes remain closed; no claim of operational readiness.
No daily DB migration, account seed, login/session API, user authorization, business API/React/worker integration, file writes or actual OCR execution.

Guards compare stored metadata, not actual file bytes, image decoding/transform correctness, canonical JSON/hash computation, current HTTP identity or supplied worker-token equality. Those remain service/storage responsibilities.
Prelock run then attempt in future mutation entry points; deadlock/serialization rollback policy and full worker acquisition/late-token behavior need C10/C13 integration tests.
Owner/asset project checks require READ COMMITTED. No blanket proof for all isolation modes, batch lock orders or production workloads.
Only macOS Python 3.12.14 and PostgreSQL 17.11 exercised. Linux/Windows, browser, real network COMMIT-response loss, file durability and backup/restore not tested.
Administrative owner/superuser DDL, trigger disabling and historical-data repair procedures are not prevented by these application guards.
